F1.title: Architecture B never received the text of any source

facts.text: The debate formatter appends source.text (runner.py line 320). Round 1 (line 121) and round 2 (line 179) both build their evidence block with this formatter.
Architecture A formats evidence with EvidencePacket.format_for_prompt (evidence.py line 109), which calls Source.content_for_prompt and returns the Exa highlights (lines 25-28).

In highlights mode the Exa request asks for highlights only (exa_retriever.py line 85), and text is stored as an empty string when Exa returns none (line 97). Retrieval mode in the results files: {'A': {'highlights': 1189}, 'B': {'highlights': 1189}}.
Committed cache: 4844 sources in 486 packets. source.text is empty for 4821. The 23 non-empty ones sit in 3 legacy packets that do not start with 'highlights__' (all legacy: True).

Applied to highlights__row0089_KXSNLHOST_ddc2b51a4839.json, the packet A read for this contract (B read row0189_KXSNLHOST_f5982df4d591, which is not committed): the A evidence block has 15396 characters and mentions 'Powell' 10 times (1 in the criteria line, 1 in a title, 8 in the highlights of 6 sources). The B block has 2411 characters and mentions 'Powell' 1 times, in a title.
Over all 458 highlights packets the median evidence block is 18449 characters for A and 2189 for B.

B's own packet (named by B's row_uid) is committed for 100 of 1189 B rows. For these rows the empty text is observed directly. For the others the claim rests on the code path and on the retrieval_mode field of the results files.
Every one of the 4 commits that touch src/resolution/debate/runner.py (ed7a36d, aaf565a, 51233b1, af93586) appends source.text in the formatter: True.

Commit bbb53ef (2026-02-17 Default Exa retrieval to highlights for architectures A/B and add A/B comparison outputs) adds the highlights field and changes A's formatter in src/retrieval/evidence.py from source.text to content_for_prompt() (line removed: True, line added: True). It does not touch src/resolution/debate/runner.py (False). B's debate code was written in commit af93586 (2026-02-10), when the retriever had no highlights mode ('highlights' in exa_retriever.py then: False) and filled source.text.
The unit test that covers the formatter builds its source with text="text" (tests/test_debate_runner.py line 49), so it passes although real packets carry their content in highlights.

facts.text: From B round-1 majority to B final: 10 correct answers became wrong, 4 wrong became correct, exact McNemar p = 0.180.

Agent-level revisions: 88 of 3567 agent-round pairs on 83 questions; correct to wrong 45, wrong to correct 43. Per model GPT-5 nano 26/16, DeepSeek V3 3/9, Llama 3.3 70B 16/18 (paper, Section 4.4.5: 88 revisions on 83 questions, 45 and 43, GPT 26/16, DeepSeek 3/9).

Totals over each file's 1,189 rows: of the net gap of 81 correct answers between A majority and B final, 75 is present after round 1 of B and 6 arises in the debate round. These are differences of totals over different row sets (see F9).
Paired on the 1153 contracts in both files: A majority 954, B round-1 majority 884, B final 878. Net gap 76, of which 70 is present after round 1.

F7.title: The search query contains the question text only, not the contract named in the criteria

facts.text: Among 1153 distinct contracts in A, 502 share their question text with another contract that differs only in the criteria, so both get the same query. Recall on YES outcomes: 56.8% for those (169 YES contracts) against 73.2% for the rest (306), Fisher exact p = 0.0003.
The query for the Glen Powell contract is built from 'Who will host Saturday Night Live Season 51?' and does not name Glen Powell.

F8.title: The evidence was retrieved months later and includes settled market pages

facts.text: The filter is Exa's end_published_date, one day after the resolution date (exa_retriever.py lines 58-60, passed at lines 67 and 84). It bounds the publication date Exa reports, not the page content.
Retrieval month of the 486 committed packets: {'2026-02': 485, '2026-01': 1}. For the 458 highlights packets the retrieval came 95-297 days after the date passed as resolution date (median 122).
957 of 4571 sources (20.9%) have no publication date, in 330 of 458 packets. The date filter cannot apply to them.

95 of 458 packets (21%) contain a prediction-market or betting page: {'metaculus.com': 11, 'fanduel': 32, 'kalshi.com': 68, 'polymarket.com': 52, 'sportsbook': 12, 'oddsshark': 3, 'predictit.org': 2, 'covers.com': 4, 'draftkings': 9, 'manifold.markets': 1}.
34 sources in 16 packets are market pages whose highlights state 'Final outcome: ...'. Examples:

'Will Monad conduct an airdrop before Oct 1, 2025?' (truth NO, A majority YES, resolution_date 2025-10-01, retrieved 2026-02-21). The packet includes https://polymarket.com/event/monad-airdrop-by/will-monad-perform-an-airdrop-by-september-30 with published_date 2025-06-26, whose highlights contain ['Final outcome: No', 'November 30']. It lists the November 25 and November 30 date markets with the outcome Yes, content written after the resolution date.

'Will Nicolás Maduro leave office next in this set?' (truth NO, A majority NO, resolution_date 2025-10-11, retrieved 2026-02-21). The packet includes https://polymarket.com/event/maduro-out-in-2025/maduro-out-by-february-28-2026 with published_date 2024-06-12, whose highlights contain ['Final outcome: Yes']. It is the market 'Maduro out by February 28, 2026' shown as settled Yes, content written after the resolution date.

'Will Nicolae Ciuca be 1st in the next Romanian presidential election first round?' (truth NO, A majority NO, resolution_date 2025-05-08, retrieved 2026-02-21). The packet includes https://polymarket.com/event/romania-presidential-election-1st-round-winner/will-nicolae-ciuc-win-the-most-votes-in-the-1st-round-of-the-romanian-presidential-election with published_date 2024-12-11, whose highlights contain ['Final outcome: No', 'George Simion100.0%']. It shows the May 2025 first round as decided (Simion at 100%). The round took place before the resolution date, so this is resolution-time information, but it was written five months after the reported publication date.
highlights__row0007_KXROMANIATOP_e3321e635fbc.json carries the same Ciuca page; this packet belongs to no row of A (False) or B (False).
15 of these 16 packets belong to rows in the A results. A's majority matches the truth on 11 of 15, so these pages are a contamination of the evidence, not a measured gain in accuracy.
